name: bell_window
revision: r1 (2026-11-10, claude/writers-mystery): written to the mystery test (STANDARDS 1.0); not voiced (the narrator voice is being changed: docs/voice_search.md)
caption: why does my village hide when I open my window 🔔
logline: Every time a boy in Saltmouth opens his bedroom window, the bell outside rings and the whole village runs indoors; tonight he leans out to catch whoever rings it.
question: why tf does the whole village hide when he opens his window?
premise: For three hundred nights, every time the boy opens his window, the village bell right outside it rings and every villager runs inside. Nobody's ever there. Mom: 'Shutters SHUT, honey.' Every morning there's an arrow in the bell post, which Mom pulls out. His is the only lit window in the village. Up on the cliff, under an old oak, something white stands all day. Tonight he leans out to catch whoever it is.
twist: Nobody rings the bell. A skeleton lives in the oak's shade on the cliff above the village (skeletons shelter from the sun) and shoots at the only player in the village whenever it sees him: the boy at his lit window. The bell hangs between the cliff and his window, so every arrow hits the bell (vanilla: a projectile rings a bell; a ringing bell sends villagers indoors). The bell was a shield. Tonight he leans out past it: the arrow rings the bell, doors slam, and the skeleton draws again, now with nothing between them. Cut.
